I would keep my land in the standard Quzhou double-cropping pattern: winter wheat followed by summer maize. I would not switch into cotton, vegetables, or other cash crops, because at my age I want a system I already know, one that matches local weather and machinery, and one that gives me steady grain income with lower management risk. Quzhou is a typical winter wheat-summer maize area, with most rainfall coming in summer and spring often dry, so this rotation fits the local water pattern and local practice well. I would plant improved winter wheat for stability and grain quality, then hybrid summer maize for yield. On wheat I would use moderate fertilizer, 3 irrigations, and 2 pesticide passes; on maize I would keep irrigation lower because summer rain does more of the work, use no-tillage after wheat harvest to save time and moisture, and keep pesticide use controlled rather than heavy. My yield target would be solid and realistic, not the absolute demonstration-field maximum. Sources I used for local context: China Agricultural University Quzhou Experimental Station on Quzhou climate and the local wheat-maize system, and reports on Quzhou “green ton-and-a-half grain” demonstration fields showing roughly 707-725 kg/mu wheat and 796-797 kg/mu maize under improved management ([climate/site](https://qzsyz.cau.edu.cn/col/col46277/index.html), [system/demonstration](https://qzsyz.cau.edu.cn/art/2024/10/8/art_46317_1039835.html), [Hebei/Ministry report](https://www.moa.gov.cn/xw/qg/202406/t20240613_6457129.htm)).
